title: Numbers Built From Given Primes

concept.title: Take the smallest number out, and push its multiples back
body: A "super ugly" number is a positive integer whose prime factors all come from a given set of primes (1 is the first such number). The numbers in increasing order are: 1, then the primes themselves, then their products, and so on. To list them in order without testing every integer, use a **min-heap** as a source of candidates: start with 1; repeatedly take the smallest number `x`, it is the next number of the list, and push `x * p` for every prime `p`.

The same number can be reached in several ways (`6 = 2 * 3 = 3 * 2`). A set of seen numbers removes the duplicates. There is also a cheaper trick: go through the primes in increasing order and **stop right after the first prime that divides `x`**. Then every number is created from exactly one smaller number, so no set is needed.

body.code:
heap = [1]
for _ in range(n):
    x = heappop(heap)                # the next number in the list
    for p in primes:                 # increasing order
        heappush(heap, x * p)
        if x % p == 0:               # a larger prime would create a duplicate
            break
print(x)

body: After `n` rounds `x` is the `n`-th number. The heap holds at most `n * k` numbers and every operation costs O(log n * k). Products stay below 10^15 here (the number is at most 10^12 and the primes at most 1000), so 64-bit integers are enough.

statement: Given `k` primes in increasing order, consider all positive integers whose prime factors are all among these primes (the number 1 is included). In increasing order they are the first, second, third number, and so on. Print the `n`-th number.
inputFormat: The second line has `k` different primes in increasing order.
constraints: The n-th number is at most 10^12.
hints: Use a min-heap that starts with 1.
Take the smallest number out and push its products with all the primes.
To avoid duplicates, stop after the first prime that divides the number taken out.

explanation: The smallest candidate is taken from a min-heap; its products with the primes are pushed, stopping after the first prime that divides it so that no number is created twice. After n rounds the last number taken is the answer.
solution.complexity: Time O(n * k * log(n * k)), space O(n * k).

code.python:
import sys
input = sys.stdin.readline

n, k = map(int, input().split())
primes = list(map(int, input().split()))

import heapq
heap = [1]
x = 1
for _ in range(n):
    x = heapq.heappop(heap)
    for p in primes:
        heapq.heappush(heap, x * p)
        if x % p == 0:
            break
print(x)
